parsed.attack: Two-sided referral dies on disclosure: to refer, a freelancer must tell a peer that they pay for a robot to phone them each morning and read out three weeks of promises they broke - an admission of being unable to work unsupervised, which is the precise reputational thing a self-employed person protects when their income depends on looking reliable. And there is no second side: the person who receives the call is the user, nobody else ever needs the app, so 'two-sided' names no mechanism. That leaves hand-recruitment from the small population that already pays a human for check-ins, at an install cost the founder cannot pay against a subscription the idea itself caps at 3% conversion.
parsed.strongest_defence: Focusmate proves accountability products spread without ad spend - r/freelance, r/productivity and indie-hacker circles discuss this constantly, because in those communities admitting the struggle is the currency rather than a stigma.
parsed.verdict_reason: The two-sided referral names no second installer and requires an admission users avoid, leaving only slow hand-recruitment from a small self-identified pool.
